items.title: [Frontend][P1] Third-party OAuth login and canonical onboarding
items.body:
## Acceptance
- [ ] Configure and integrate at least one real supported third-party provider (e.g. Google) using existing Kratos/Hydra boundaries in #40.
- [ ] Provider callback, cancellation/errors and supported new/returning user onboarding work end to end.
- [ ] Define safe identity linking; email matches alone must not silently claim an existing account.
- [ ] Secrets remain outside committed/browser configuration; provide review setup instructions.
- [ ] Demonstrate real third-party authentication; Hydra email/password OAuth flow alone does not satisfy this requirement.

## Dependencies / related
#66 #40.

## Working agreement
Implement one focused ticket at a time using a separate prompt. Inspect the current repository and reuse existing code/contracts before changes. Preserve user changes. Source changes and logical commits remain local; no push. Report verification and limitations on this issue; do not claim mocks or unpushed work is remotely complete.
Use the specified Next.js App Router/React Compiler/TypeScript/Tailwind 4/ESLint/Bun project stack. HeroUI v3 dark theme is the UI baseline; compose existing components first, otherwise match its tokens and accessible behavior. Responsive layout, keyboard support, useful validation and loading/empty/error states are part of each relevant UI task.

## Shared icon convention — Lucide
Use **Lucide** via `lucide-react` as the shared custom UI icon library. Install/reuse one compatible stable version with the Bun lockfile; use direct named imports, consistent size/stroke width and `currentColor` to match HeroUI v3 dark-theme tokens. Decorative icons are hidden from assistive technology; icon-only controls have an accessible name on the control. Do not use emoji/text glyphs as UI icons, load icons through an external API/CDN, import the whole icon namespace, or add another custom UI icon library. Keep HeroUI's built-in internal icons and authentic provider/brand logos where appropriate. Do not add icons where they do not improve the UI.

## Design and dynamic UX acceptance — 2026-10-06
Shared visual/interaction/rendering contract: #94. Apply within this ticket's existing scope and dependencies; keep HeroUI v3 dark theme and Lucide.

- [ ] Show provider redirect/callback progress, cancellation and actionable safe failures in the shared auth design; allow a deliberate retry without duplicate identity creation.
- [ ] Keep callback pages request-specific and noindex; do not place authorization codes or identity secrets in metadata or diagnostic UI.

## Current baseline and delivery process — 2026-10-06
Follow #94's approved-baseline/process section. Build on the owner-approved #61 correction (remote dev aef4673) and #62 typed transport; keep HeroUI v3 dark theme and Lucide. Choose the page composition and responsive presentation independently. Earlier layout examples are suggestions; functional requirements, real data, security and accessible interactions remain acceptance criteria.
For visual changes, inspect the running app before/after at desktop/mobile, refine the first pass and report screenshots plus real interaction/error-state evidence. Update affected smoke checks rather than freezing temporary page text/header geometry. Reuse #62 and register/validate required operations; its current /graphql endpoint does not already support every future operation.
Use one ticket + one prompt, update existing relevant project items In Progress → Testing after verification, report actual checks/limitations and keep logical commits local for owner review/manual push. See #94 for details.

### Integration focus
Reuse the canonical #40/#66 callback/session handling rather than a second OAuth implementation. Real provider redirects and onboarding outcomes require live evidence.


## Reference implementation notes (optional; 2026-10-12)

Reference: user-supplied `i-love-shopping2-main.zip`, rooted at `i-love-shopping2/` (not part of this repository). Useful files to inspect if available:
- `frontend/src/components/GoogleButton.tsx`
- `frontend/src/api/auth.ts`
- `backend/src/main/java/com/iloveshopping/auth/GoogleTokenVerifier.java`

Reference provider onboarding/error UX only. Keep OAuth/OIDC via Hydra/Kratos and secure callback/state handling; never replace with frontend token trust or bespoke backend social-login verification.

**Agent decision rule:** Inspect the current ByteCore code, existing tests and related issues **before** implementation. Treat these references as behavioral examples, not mandatory code. If an existing implementation already meets the acceptance criteria (or is better integrated), retain it and supply evidence rather than rewrite it. Implement only missing requirements; avoid unrelated refactoring, preserve architecture and owner changes. If the reference archive is unavailable to the agent, proceed from the actual repository contracts without guessing reference contents.

items.title: Adopt the cuprum release process: publish the sdist and make releases idempotent (6.3.1)
items.body:
## Summary

[leynos/cuprum#488](https://github.com/leynos/cuprum/pull/488) is the reference for how our Python packages are released: sdist plus wheels, attested, published idempotently to PyPI under Trusted Publishing, and mirrored to a draft-then-published GitHub Release. falcon-correlate must adopt it before it publishes to PyPI. Roadmap task 6.3.1 ("Configure build and publish workflow") is the place it lands.

[leynos/polythene#154](https://github.com/leynos/polythene/pull/154) (merged as `ae72080`) has already ported the process to a pure-Python project, so it is the closer model here; cuprum's `release.yml` on `main` remains the live reference.

## Current state

- **Build:** `.github/actions/pure-python-wheel/action.yml` runs `uv build --wheel` and uploads only `*.whl`. No sdist is built or checked in CI. `make build-release` builds both with `python -m build --sdist --wheel`, which is a different front end from the one CI uses.
- **The current workflow ships empty releases.** `release.yml` downloads with `actions/download-artifact@v8` and `path: dist`, then uploads `find dist/wheels-* … | xargs -0 -r gh release upload`. Since v8 that glob matches nothing, and `xargs -r` makes the empty match silent. The [v0.1.0 run](https://github.com/leynos/falcon-correlate/actions/runs/32640953655) logged `find: 'dist/wheels-*': No such file or directory`, succeeded, and the [v0.1.0 release](https://github.com/leynos/falcon-correlate/releases/tag/v0.1.0) has no assets. This is the same defect as [leynos/lading#256](https://github.com/leynos/lading/issues/256).
- **Publication:** `softprops/action-gh-release@v3` creates and publishes the release before any asset is attached. Nothing goes to PyPI, and `falcon-correlate` does not exist there. Yet `README.md`, `docs/quickstart.md` and `docs/users-guide.md` all tell readers to `pip install falcon-correlate`.
- **Versions:** `pyproject.toml` says `0.2.0` and `CHANGELOG.md` has a `0.2.0 - 2026-08-27` entry, but no `v0.2.0` tag or release exists.
- **Hardening gaps:**
  - `contents: write` is granted to every job at the top level.
  - Concurrency uses `cancel-in-progress: true`, so a re-pushed tag can cancel a running upload.
  - `${{ github.ref_name }}` is interpolated straight into a `run:` script.
  - Checkouts persist credentials.
  - Third-party actions are referenced by mutable tags.
- **Unused matrix:** `.github/workflows/build-wheels.yml` and `.github/actions/build-wheels/` (cibuildwheel across Linux, macOS and Windows) are not called by any workflow. The project has no native code.
- **Docs and tests:**
  - `docs/developers-guide.md` mentions the release jobs only in the runner table and has no release section.
  - Four ADRs exist, so the next is ADR-005.
  - `tests/workflow_contracts/` already holds workflow contract tests.

## Required adoption

Mirror the merged process, adapting it only where this project differs. falcon-correlate is pure Python with the `uv_build` backend.

1. **One sdist and one wheel on every build.** The composite action runs plain `uv build --out-dir dist`. That builds the sdist first and the wheel from it, so every run proves the sdist is buildable. Both files travel in the `wheels-pure` artefact, uploaded with `if-no-files-found: error`. Delete the unused cibuildwheel workflow and action, as polythene did, and make `make build-release` use the same `uv build`.
2. **Exactly one sdist, checked on pull requests.** A `ci.yml` build job runs the action on pull requests and fails unless exactly one sdist and one wheel are present, rather than failing at tag time.
3. **Version check.** A `check-version` job compares the tag with `pyproject.toml` as an exact string (`v0.2.0` matches `0.2.0`) and reports whether the version is a pre-release. Every job that attests, uploads or releases waits on it.
4. **Attestation.** An `attest` job collects every wheel and exactly one sdist and refuses anything else. It attests them with `actions/attest-build-provenance`, names the Sigstore bundle after the tag alone so that a re-run adds no further asset, and hands everything on as one `release-dist` artefact. Every later job then ships the attested bytes.
5. **Idempotent PyPI publication.**
   - `publish-pypi` runs in a `pypi` environment and holds only `contents: read` and `id-token: write`.
   - It reads the Simple index with a retrying, time-limited `curl`. A 404 for an unpublished project means nothing is skipped; any other HTTP error fails the run.
   - It drops every filename the index already has and uploads the rest through `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` with `skip-existing: true` under Trusted Publishing.
   - When nothing is left, the upload is skipped and the job succeeds. No PyPI token is stored.
6. **Draft-then-publish GitHub Release, without `--clobber`.**
   - `draft-release` creates or reuses the tag's draft. This replaces `softprops/action-gh-release`, which publishes too early.
   - `publish-release` runs only after PyPI holds every artefact. It uploads only the assets the release lacks, taking PyPI's bytes for any name PyPI already holds.
   - It then checks that both destinations hold the same digests and un-drafts the release, marking it as a pre-release when the version is one.
   - An empty artefact set is a failed run, never an empty release. Port `scripts/release_assets.py`, `scripts/release_assets_cli.py` and `scripts/release_version.py` from polythene.
7. **Hardening.**
   - `permissions: {}` at the top level, with per-job grants.
   - `persist-credentials: false` on every checkout, including inside the composite action.
   - `cancel-in-progress: false`.
   - Third-party actions pinned to full commit SHAs.
   - Every workflow value reaches `run:` scripts through `env:` as a quoted variable, under `set -euo pipefail`.
8. **Tests for the checked-in release steps.** Port polythene's tests into `tests/workflow_contracts/` or alongside it:
   - `test_release_workflow_contract.py`: job scopes, environment, concurrency, ordering, pinned actions, and the scan of every `run:` script for `${{`.
   - `test_release_publish_steps.py`, `test_release_github_steps.py` and `test_release_reconciliation.py`: the step scripts run against recording `gh` and `curl` stand-ins.
   - `test_ci_wheel_build.py`: the pull-request check with zero, one and two sdists.

   Cover collecting the sdist with every wheel, failing without an sdist, skipping published names, uploading only what remains, and succeeding when nothing is left.
9. **Documentation.** Add a "Publishing a release" section to `docs/developers-guide.md`, with a settings section listing the manual repository settings. On GitHub, the `pypi` environment is restricted to `v*.*.*` tags. On PyPI, the Trusted Publisher is bound to that environment.

## falcon-correlate-specific adaptations

- **PyPI project.** Register the `falcon-correlate` PyPI project and its Trusted Publisher before the first tag: owner `leynos`, repository `falcon-correlate`, workflow `release.yml`, environment `pypi`. The name currently returns 404; if it cannot be claimed, choose a distribution name as polythene did with `polythene-isolate`, keeping the import package `falcon_correlate`.
- **Install check.** The pull-request build should install the built wheel into a clean environment and import `falcon_correlate` without the `celery` or `httpx` extras, guarding ADR-004's promise that importing the package does not pull in Celery.
- **Telemetry.** Drop cuprum's `release-telemetry` steps, as polythene did, unless this project adopts cuprum's ADR-014 sink.

## Decisions to record

- **First release.**
  - Decide whether the untagged `0.2.0` changelog entry (dated 2026-08-27) is re-dated and shipped through the new pipeline as the first PyPI release.
  - Decide whether the asset-less v0.1.0 GitHub release gets its wheel back-filled or a note in `CHANGELOG.md` instead.
- **ADR-005** recording the release pipeline and the GitHub Release as a second destination reconciled with PyPI. Model it on cuprum's ADR-017 and polythene's ADR-002.
- **Docs to update.**
  - `docs/falcon-correlation-id-middleware-design.md` gains a packaging and release section.
  - `README.md`, `docs/quickstart.md` and `docs/users-guide.md` get their installation instructions checked against the published name.
  - Roadmap 6.3.1 has its "Configure build and publish workflow" box ticked.

## Acceptance

- A tagged release publishes the sdist and the wheel to PyPI and attaches the same bytes, plus the provenance bundle, to the GitHub Release.
- Re-running the same tag completes successfully without uploading anything new.
- A release run that finds no artefacts fails instead of publishing an empty release.
- A pull request whose build lacks an sdist fails CI.
- The release-step tests pass under `make test`.

## References

- [leynos/cuprum#488](https://github.com/leynos/cuprum/pull/488) (the reference implementation), with cuprum's `docs/adr-017-release-pipeline.md` and `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- [leynos/polythene#154](https://github.com/leynos/polythene/pull/154) (the pure-Python port), with polythene's `docs/adr-002-attested-reconciled-release-pipeline.md`
- [leynos/lading#256](https://github.com/leynos/lading/issues/256) (the same empty-release defect)
- Sibling adoption issues: [leynos/femtologging#538](https://github.com/leynos/femtologging/issues/538) and [leynos/cmd-mox#320](https://github.com/leynos/cmd-mox/issues/320)

items.title: docs(readme): replayable README rebuild brief — experience voice, kernel vs third-party apps (#1981), packages/SDK/plugin, link-not-explain
items.body:
## What this is
A **replayable brief** for regenerating the root `README.md` — not a one-shot rewrite. The README is the front door of the repo and it drifts every time positioning, the kernel/app boundary, or the package set moves. This issue holds the *inputs, skeleton, and rules*; each replay regenerates the README from them, opens a PR, and posts a run-log comment here. **Keep this issue open.** Re-run whenever a trigger below fires.

## Why now
The current README is written in the frame we're leaving:
- **Protocol/infrastructure voice** — ima-jin/imajin-ai#1376 moves the site to experience voice (*You compose. Imajin orchestrates. Signed. Legible.*); the README should be the same voice, same frame.
- **Kernel carries the verticals** — `coffee`, `dykil`, `links`, `learn`, `events`, `market` are presented as parts of Imajin. Under ima-jin/imajin-ai#1981 they are **third-party apps behind a registered-app contract**; the kernel is the six primitives + the rails that serve them. The README should read that way *before* the extraction lands, not after.
- **Five primitives** — Revocation is the sixth (#2027).
- **Packages / plugin / SDK** are stale — 29 workspace packages, SDK publishing in flight (#1982, ima-jin/imajin-ai#1581, ima-jin/imajin-ai#1011, ima-jin/imajin-ai#1992), OpenClaw plugin surface (`nanoclaw-imajin-channel`, `openclaw-infer-passthrough`, `openclaw-reflex-guard`, `claw-envelope`, `claw-provisioner`) barely mentioned.
- **App-specific flows in the root** — "Auth Flow" and "Payment Flow" sections belong to the services that own them. Root README links; it does not explain.

## Inputs (order of authority — read these, not the old README)
1. `biz-dev/positioning-speed-of-thought-signed.md` + `tools/context/framing.md` (workspace) — voice, hero, hooks. Canonical per ima-jin/imajin-ai#1376.
2. The six-primitive grammar — *Artifact · The Governing Grammar* v1.3 / *Identity Primitives — A Manual* v0.1 (see ima-jin/imajin-ai#2027 for the shape). Kernel = these six + rails.
3. ima-jin/imajin-ai#1981 — the registered-app contract. Apps are services the kernel *serves*, registered as identities (#1990). Language: "apps built on Imajin," never "Imajin's apps."
4. **Live repo state, not memory:** `apps/*` for the app list, `packages/*/package.json` for the package table (name, description, publish status). Generated, never hand-typed.
5. ima-jin/imajin-ai#1982 / ima-jin/imajin-ai#1581 / ima-jin/imajin-ai#1011 / ima-jin/imajin-ai#1992 — SDK publish status. Say honestly what is `npm install`-able vs workspace-only.
6. ima-jin/imajin-ai#1427 — the honest-record promise ("A note on use") stays, and stays accurate.
7. `imajin-app-template` (org repo) — the "build an app" pointer.

## Target skeleton (v1 — revise here when it changes)
1. **Hero** — *You compose. Imajin orchestrates. Signed. Legible.* One paragraph in experience voice. Secondary hook: *the speed of thought, signed.*
2. **What it is** — the kernel: six primitives (Attestation · Communication · Attribution · Settlement · Discovery · Revocation) + the rails that serve them. Proof of history, not proof of work — two lines, link to whitepaper for the rest.
3. **What you can do today** — experience voice, concrete, dated. No roadmap bleed.
4. **Kernel vs. apps** — the boundary as a sentence, then a table: each app in `apps/*` → one line → **link to that app's own README.** Apps are third-party services under the registered-app contract (#1981); a node operator runs the kernel, not a calendar.
5. **Build an app** — registered-app contract, `imajin-app-template`, the SDK packages an app actually needs. Link, don't explain.
6. **Packages (SDK)** — generated table from `packages/*/package.json`: name · one-liner · published/workspace-only. Plugin surface called out as its own group (OpenClaw plugin, channel, infer-passthrough, reflex-guard, envelope, provisioner).
7. **Run a node** — quick start for the *kernel only*. Deployment → link to docs.
8. **Docs / RFCs / spec** — pointers, incl. conformance (#1287) and the two-entity note.
9. **Contributing · Security · A note on use · License** — carried forward; "A note on use" reconciled with ima-jin/imajin-ai#1427.

**Dropped from root (moved or linked):** Auth Flow, Payment Flow, per-app port tables (3100+/7100+, 3400+/7400+), Identity Model detail (→ docs), Protocol Matrix (→ docs or whitepaper), First Event (historical → build-log with date), Project Status (→ replaced by dated "today" section).

## Rules for every replay
- Voice inherits from the positioning frame. Zero occurrences of "Imajin runs your community" or any subject-grammar where the system is the actor and the human is the object.
- Six primitives, named, every time.
- Apps described as third-party services; each app row links to a README the app *owns*. If an app has no README, the replay **creates a stub** (name, what it does, how it registers with the kernel, link back) — root README never carries app internals.
- Package table generated from `package.json`, with an honest publish column. No `npm install @imajin/x` instruction for anything not actually published.
- No roadmap in present tense. Anything not shipped is dated or omitted.
- Historical claims get a date, not a silent rewrite.
- PR title `docs(readme): replay <YYYY-MM-DD> — <trigger>`; PR body links this issue; on merge, post a run-log comment here: date · merge commit · trigger · what changed in skeleton/rules (if anything).

## Replay triggers
- ima-jin/imajin-ai#1376 positioning frame changes (hero, hooks, voice).
- ima-jin/imajin-ai#1981 lands an extraction or changes the contract.
- A package is published/unpublished (#1982), added, or removed.
- An app is added/removed/moved out of the monorepo.
- A primitive is added, renamed, or re-ruled (#2027 is the first).
- "A note on use" or Security changes (#1427).

## Known gaps at first replay (2026-09-05, `origin/main` 87b5434)
- `apps/`: 9 apps, **1** has a README (`events`). 8 stubs to create.
- `packages/`: 29 packages, **9** have READMEs. Table generation covers this; stubs optional.
- SDK not yet published → package table says workspace-only until ima-jin/imajin-ai#1982 closes.
- Root README is 362 lines / 18KB — target is materially shorter; depth lives one link away.

## Acceptance (per replay)
- README regenerated from the inputs above, not edited from the previous version.
- Every app row resolves to an app-owned README.
- Package table matches `packages/*/package.json` at the PR's commit.
- `git grep -iE "five primitives|runs your community" README.md` → nothing.
- Run-log comment posted here.

## Related
Parent ima-jin/imajin-ai#1376 · ima-jin/imajin-ai#1981 kernel/app split · ima-jin/imajin-ai#1990 app registry · ima-jin/imajin-ai#1982 / ima-jin/imajin-ai#1581 / ima-jin/imajin-ai#1011 / ima-jin/imajin-ai#1992 SDK publishing · ima-jin/imajin-ai#2027 sixth primitive · ima-jin/imajin-ai#1427 honest-record promise · ima-jin/imajin-ai#1287 conformance · `imajin-app-template`.

items.title: Feature: remote capture from phone — voice notes, images & links + thoughts via direct-to-intake

milestone.title: Remote capture & phone
milestone.description: Theme H/J: capture from the phone (voice, images, links, directives) reliably over the LAN — including hardening the capture pipeline under the GUI+serve threading model.

items.body:
## Context

Capture ideas away from the desktop: send a voice note, an image, or a link (e.g. an Instagram post URL) **plus some accompanying thoughts** from a phone, and have grandplan organize it into a note like any hotkey capture — media preserved as attachments, URLs preserved as link resources.

Transport decision: **direct-to-intake** — a phone shortcut / minimal PWA that POSTs to the existing HTTP intake (`src/grandplan/adapters/http_intake.py`) over a private network (Tailscale/WireGuard or LAN). No messenger platform in the loop: content never transits a third-party cloud, so the offline/zero-egress invariant holds end-to-end (QAS-1). The core app still never makes an outbound request.

Much of this exists already:
- `http_intake.py` — token-authed (constant-time), 127.0.0.1-default intake built exactly for "POST content from a phone over LAN/VPN".
- `voice.py` — offline STT via `faster-whisper` (`grandplan[voice]`); mic-based today, but the same local model transcribes an audio *file*.
- The organizer's `resources` pipeline already extracts URLs present in the capture text into the note's `## Resources` block (with the anti-hallucination containment check), so "thoughts + IG link" → link lands in the note with no new code.

## Threads

- **Attachments over intake** — accept media alongside text (multipart or size-capped base64 field; current 1 MiB body cap must be rethought for voice notes/images, with an explicit new cap). Persist media into a vault attachments dir; reference from the note as `file` resources. Reject unexpected content types; never execute/render untrusted content.
- **Voice-note transcription** — route received audio files through a file-based `Transcriber` (reuse `faster-whisper`, local, offline). Transcript becomes the capture text (plus any typed thoughts); original audio kept as an attachment (lossless: the source artifact is preserved).
- **Image + thoughts (v1)** — store the image as an attachment resource; the accompanying text is the capture. (v2, deferred: optional local vision model to describe/extract — new multi-GB model on the 16 GB no-GPU target, needs its own evaluation.)
- **Phone-side sender** — an iOS/Android Shortcut recipe and/or a single-file PWA served by the intake (share-sheet friendly: share a post/photo/voice memo → adds thoughts → POST). Documented setup for Tailscale/WireGuard reachability.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A voice note POSTed from a phone becomes an organized note whose body is the local transcript; the audio file is saved in the vault and linked as a resource.
- [ ] An image + text POST becomes a note with the image attached and linked.
- [ ] Text containing a URL (e.g. an Instagram post) yields a note with that URL in `## Resources` (existing behavior verified through the new path).
- [ ] Intake stays token-gated and 127.0.0.1 by default; media size/type limits enforced before reading the body; auth failures leak nothing.
- [ ] Zero network egress from grandplan itself — nothing is fetched; the app only receives. Fully offline processing (Whisper local).
- [ ] Works on the 16 GB / no-GPU target.

## Non-goals (for this issue)

- Messenger-platform bridges (Telegram/WhatsApp bots). Considered and deferred: they route content through third-party clouds; if ever built, it would be a separate optional companion process, never core.
- Vision-model understanding of images (v2 candidate).
- Fetching remote content from shared URLs (violates zero-egress; the link itself is the artifact).

## Related

- Sits after the capture-latency work (#34 and the pipeline call-count reduction) — remote capture feeds the same organize pipeline, so per-note speed lands first.
- Media/attachment groundwork may inform #36 (converse with the vault) retrieval over transcripts.

items.title: feat(auth): connect Hermex directly to Craft servers

labels.name: area:platform
labels.description: Additional Apple platforms and platform requests

items.body:
## Problem

Hermex currently assumes every configured server is `hermes-webui`: HTTP(S) REST endpoints, password/session-cookie authentication, and SSE chat streams. A user needs Hermex to connect directly to a self-hosted Craft Agents server without a compatibility relay.

Craft uses a distinct WebSocket RPC protocol. Treating its token as a Hermes password or entering a `ws://` URL in the existing Hermes form cannot work and would make failures misleading.

## Verified Craft contract

Verified against the local `craft-agents-oss` checkout on 2026-09-07:

- Headless entry: `packages/server/src/index.ts`
- Transport: `ws://` or `wss://`
- Default bind: `127.0.0.1:9100`
- Authentication handshake:
  ```json
  {
    "id": "<uuid>",
    "type": "handshake",
    "protocolVersion": "1.0",
    "token": "<CRAFT_SERVER_TOKEN>"
  }
  ```
- Success is a `handshake_ack`; invalid credentials return an error/close.
- Craft's smoke coverage is in `packages/server/src/__tests__/smoke.test.ts`.
- Plain `ws://` is acceptable only for localhost development. Remote servers require `wss://`.

Exact session, message, streaming-event, reconnect, and cancellation envelopes must be verified from Craft's typed RPC transport/handlers immediately before each implementation slice. Do not infer them from the Hermes contract.

## Scope

Add Craft as an explicit server kind and build a native Craft transport boundary alongside the existing Hermes API client.

### Slice 1: connection and authentication

- Add an explicit `Hermes` / `Craft` server kind to configured server identity.
- Add a Craft connection form using WebSocket URL plus server token.
- Store the Craft token in Keychain, keyed by canonical server identity.
- Perform the real Craft `1.0` handshake before reporting success.
- Allow `ws://localhost`, `ws://127.0.0.1`, and simulator-to-host development addresses intentionally supported by the app; reject unencrypted non-local remote endpoints.
- Map DNS, TLS, timeout, protocol-version, and credential failures to distinct user-facing errors.
- Never log or persist the token outside Keychain.
- Preserve existing Hermes onboarding and configured servers without migration regressions.

### Follow-on slices in the same integration

- Typed Craft RPC request/response codec with tolerant decoding.
- Session list and session history parity.
- Start, steer, stop, and resume session flows.
- Streaming event handling, reconnect, replay/deduplication, and app foreground recovery.
- Workspace browsing and supported system entry points.
- Explicit capability gating for unsupported Hermes-only and Craft-only features.

## Acceptance criteria for Slice 1

- A local Craft server at `ws://127.0.0.1:9100` can be added from the simulator with a valid token.
- Invalid tokens and incompatible protocol responses do not create or activate a server.
- Non-local `ws://` is rejected before credentials are transmitted.
- Craft credentials, selections, and state do not appear under a Hermes server or another Craft server.
- Removing a Craft server removes its local credential and state using the existing removal semantics.
- Existing Hermes login, server switching, and persistence tests remain green.
- Focused URL-policy, handshake, cancellation, timeout, and Keychain-isolation tests are included.
- A signed Debug build is manually exercised on iPhone 17; both valid and invalid Craft login paths are checked.

## Non-goals

- No Hermex-hosted relay or backend.
- No conversion of Craft into the Hermes REST/SSE contract.
- No enterprise identity provider invented in the mobile client. OIDC/SAML belongs at an explicit, verified server or reverse-proxy contract.

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

0.144.1, 0.144.0, & 0.142.5

### What subscription do you have?

plus

### Which model were you using?

Openrouter Models

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Git bash

### Codex doctor report

```json
Tip: New Build faster with Codex.


› codex doctor --json


■ {"error":{"message":"No endpoints found that support the native `namespace` tool
type. To learn more about provider routing, visit:
https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/provider-selection","code":400}}
```

### What issue are you seeing?

# Custom Responses provider intermittently fails with native `namespace` tool routing errors

## Summary

Codex CLI intermittently renders a previously working OpenRouter custom-provider profile unusable due to native/proprietary namespace tool routing errors.

OpenRouter rejects the request before model generation with:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "No endpoints found that support the native `namespace` tool type. To learn more about provider routing, visit: https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/provider-selection",
    "code": 400
  }
}
```

This happens even for ordinary prompts that do not request MCP tools, plugins, apps, connectors, collaboration, or subagents.

The same OpenRouter account, API key, Codex profile, repository, and model previously worked extensively. My OpenRouter dashboard records approximately:

* 67.5 million tokens
* 736 requests
* Codex as the application
* successful usage across multiple OpenRouter models

This was an established working development workflow, not an experimental configuration that never functioned.

## Environment

* OS: Windows 11
* Shell: Git Bash / MINGW64
* Provider: OpenRouter
* Wire API: Responses
* Model: `tencent/hy3:free`
* Profile: `~/.codex/hy3_openrouter.config.toml`
* Codex versions reproduced:
 
  * `0.144.1`
  * `0.144.0`
  * `0.142.5`
* Authentication: `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`

Relevant redacted profile shape:

```toml
model_provider = "openrouter"
model = "tencent/hy3:free"
model_reasoning_effort = "high"
model_context_window = 262144
model_supports_reasoning_summaries = false

[model_providers.openrouter]
name = "OpenRouter"
base_url = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"
env_key = "OPENROUTER_API_KEY"
wire_api = "responses"
```

The profile is definitely being loaded. Codex displays:

```text
OpenAI Codex (v0.142.5)
model: tencent/hy3:free high
```

Codex also prints:

```text
Model metadata for `tencent/hy3:free` not found. Defaulting to fallback metadata;
this can degrade performance and cause issues.
```

That warning was also present during a session in which model generation and shell tool calls worked, so it is not itself the fatal error.

## Reproduction

Launch Codex using the OpenRouter profile:

```bash
codex --profile hy3_openrouter
```

Send any prompt, including a plain text prompt or a normal repository task.

Codex immediately returns:

```text
No endpoints found that support the native `namespace` tool type.
```

The model never processes the prompt.

## Exact-version reproduction

To eliminate PATH ambiguity, I launched Codex 0.142.5 directly:

```bash
npx -y @openai/codex@0.142.5 --version
npx -y @openai/codex@0.142.5 --profile hy3_openrouter
```

The version command returned:

```text
codex-cli 0.142.5
```

The TUI also confirmed:

```text
OpenAI Codex (v0.142.5)
```

The same native `namespace` error occurred.

This means the failure is not limited to Codex 0.144.x.

## Intermittent successful session

During one Codex 0.142.5 session using the same profile, the request successfully reached the model.

The model generated and attempted multiple shell calls, including:

```text
git status
git branch --show-current
git log --oneline -5
echo hello
```

Some Git commands were separately rejected by the Windows sandbox policy, but:

```text
echo hello
```

executed successfully and returned output.

That proves the following worked during that session:

* Codex contacted OpenRouter.
* OpenRouter routed the request to a model endpoint.
* The model generated a response.
* Codex received tool calls.
* Codex entered its normal tool-execution loop.

After exiting and launching a fresh session with the same Codex 0.142.5 binary and the same profile, the first prompt again failed before generation with the native `namespace` routing error.

The result therefore varies across launches despite the same binary and profile. Possible explanations include differences in the effective outbound tool set, persisted or dynamically registered capabilities, or OpenRouter’s upstream endpoint selection. I have not isolated which variable accounts for the intermittency.

## Attempted feature reduction

I also launched Codex while disabling the obvious features that could introduce namespace tools, including multi-agent, collaboration, apps/connectors, plugins, MCP-related app support, tool search, and MCP elicitation.

Codex emitted deprecation warnings such as:

```text
[features].collab is deprecated. Use [features].multi_agent instead.

[features].connectors is deprecated. Use [features].apps instead.
```

The replacement feature names were also disabled.

The request still failed with the exact same error:

```text
No endpoints found that support the native `namespace` tool type.
```

This suggests that the condition triggering the `namespace` routing error may involve:

* another built-in Codex tool path;
* tool registration independent of the expected feature flags;
* persistent plugin, MCP, app, or session state;
* or a tool that remains serialized after its associated feature has been disabled.

## Actual behavior

The request appears to contain, or is being interpreted as containing, a native namespace tool.

OpenRouter rejects the request during endpoint selection before an underlying inference provider processes the prompt.

The error does not identify:

* the rejected namespace name;
* which Codex feature registered it;
* whether it came from MCP, a plugin, an app, collaboration, or another built-in tool;
* the effective outbound tool list;
* or a supported configuration option that disables or flattens namespace tools.

Because every OpenRouter model profile passes through the same Responses routing layer, multiple unrelated models fail with the same error.

## Expected behavior

For custom providers configured with:

```toml
wire_api = "responses"
```

Codex should not assume support for proprietary native namespace tools.

Codex should do one or more of the following:

1. Default custom Responses providers to standard function tools.

2. Flatten namespace tools into uniquely named top-level function tools.

3. Omit optional namespace tools unless the provider explicitly advertises support.

4. Provide a documented provider capability setting such as:

   ```toml
   namespace_tools = false
   ```

5. Ensure that disabling a feature removes its corresponding namespace from the serialized request.

6. Produce a deterministic outbound tool set for identical versions, profiles, and sessions.

7. Report the exact namespace and originating feature when a provider rejects it.

8. Expose the final serialized tool list through debug logging or `codex doctor`.

More generally, protocol selection and capability negotiation should be independent. Configuring a provider to use the Responses API should not, by itself, imply support for proprietary namespace tool types.

## Impact

This failure blocks all Codex work through the affected OpenRouter profiles, including simple prompts that do not use advanced tooling.

Changing the prompt does not help because the request is rejected before generation.

Switching among OpenRouter models does not help because the common request envelope is rejected before an underlying endpoint is selected.

The failure caused the sudden loss of an established workflow that had already processed tens of millions of tokens successfully.

Users should not need to:

* downgrade several Codex releases;
* repeatedly recreate sessions;
* guess at undocumented feature combinations;
* disable unrelated functionality;
* inspect internal HTTP payloads;
* or build a localhost request-rewriting proxy

to make Codex send a compatible Responses request.

## Requested investigation

Please determine:

1. Whether the serialized request contains a native `namespace` tool and, if so, which tool and feature introduced it.
2. Why the same 0.142.5 binary and profile can succeed in one session and fail after relaunch.
3. Whether fallback model metadata affects provider capability or tool selection.
4. Whether disabled features are actually removed from the serialized request.
5. Whether plugins, apps, MCP servers, cached model metadata, or session state dynamically alter the tool schema.
6. Why custom Responses-provider requests trigger native namespace-tool routing without explicit capability opt-in.
7. Whether Codex can flatten namespace tools automatically for generic Responses providers.
8. Whether Codex can expose the effective outbound request tool list in diagnostic output.
9. Whether Codex currently conflates protocol selection (wire_api = "responses") with capability assumptions (such as native namespace tool support) for third-party Responses providers.
> I am happy to refine the approach based on maintainer feedback.
## Related issues

This appears related to:

* #23186 — Codex wraps MCP tools in `type: "namespace"` for custom/local providers.
* #26234 — proposal to flatten namespace tools for OpenRouter, Ollama, and LM Studio.
* #31875 — custom/Azure Responses failure caused by Codex-specific collaboration namespace tooling.

This report adds two important observations:

1. The same Codex 0.142.5 binary and profile can alternate between successful model tool execution and complete pre-generation rejection.
2. Disabling the obvious namespace-producing feature groups does not prevent OpenRouter from receiving or detecting a native namespace tool.


### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Configure an OpenRouter model provider with `wire_api = "responses"`.
2. Launch Codex using a profile that selects that provider.
3. Submit any prompt.
4. Observe that OpenRouter rejects the request before model generation with the native `namespace` tool routing error.

### What is the expected behavior?

Custom providers using the Responses API should be able to process ordinary prompts without Codex requiring support for proprietary native `namespace` tools. Unsupported optional tools should be omitted or flattened into standard function tools unless the provider explicitly advertises native namespace support.


### Additional information

_No response_

items.body:
Replaces #221 (and #177 before it). Part of the v0.5 epic #220. Liam approved this shape on 2026-10-27; the Feishu adapter package is named `vela-lark` (Liam, 2026-10-27).

**Friday: post a plan on this issue first; Claude reviews it before any code. Forge reviews the PRs.**

## Why (long-term maintenance and extension, not this migration's size)

What will keep growing:
- The channel layer is Vela's main line: #171 external events, #217 topic ↔ group hand-off, third-party platforms on the standard interface.
- Built-in extensions will be rebuilt (memory, #218) and other people will write extensions.
- Other front ends may come (an app, the v0.6 setup wizard). They need the SDK but not the terminal UI.
- Most code is written by bots. They often route around conventions and lint; they cannot route around a package dependency that isn't declared. Small packages with a clear public surface also mean less context per change.

What pi does (checked, pi-mono `842c731`, 1.4.0): packages are cut by "who uses it on its own, and what dependencies it carries" (`pi-ai`, `pi-agent-core`, `pi-tui`, `pi-mcp`, `pi-codemode`; the product `pi-coding-agent` depends on them). Each package's `exports` map is its contract, and scripts guard it (`scripts/check-entry-graphs.mjs`: "Entry points are cost contracts", a load budget per entry; `scripts/check-runtime-deps.mjs`: runtime imports must be declared). Workspaces hoist dependencies, so undeclared imports still resolve. Package boundaries alone don't hold without a check.

Why not the earlier shapes: three packages put the channel runtime in a grab-bag "extensions" package with Feishu, memory, rag and mcp, so a third-party platform would have to install the Feishu SDK; two packages kept the SDK tied to the terminal UI and avoided defining core's public surface.

## Shape

Bun workspaces (`"workspaces": ["packages/*"]`, `workspace:*` between packages), one version for all packages, one release script that publishes in dependency order. Dependencies only point down:

```
@glows777/vela            CLI / TUI / vela serve / setup; the package users install; re-exports the others
  ├─ @glows777/vela-lark        Feishu/Lark adapter (the Feishu SDK lives only here)
  │    └─ @glows777/vela-channels  channel runtime + standard platform interface
  │                                (gateway, topics, routines, recovery, directory; home of #171 and #217)
  ├─ @glows777/vela-mcp         MCP (MCP SDK)
  ├─ @glows777/vela-rag         RAG (sqlite-vec native module + embeddings)
  └─ @glows777/vela-core        SDK: agent, session, context, tools, models, auth, prompt, config, usage,
                                skills, images, extension API, testing, and the light built-ins
                                memory, web, permission-gate
```

One rule decides package boundaries: **a separate package only for a different consumer or a different heavy dependency.**
- `vela-core`: everyone; carries only ai-sdk, zod, yaml, diff and similar. Other front ends depend on this alone.
- `vela-channels`: consumed by platform adapters and `vela serve`. A third-party platform depends on it, never on the Lark adapter.
- `vela-lark`: the Feishu SDK (`@larksuiteoapi/node-sdk`, 29 MB installed) is used only in `extensions/feishu/transport.ts` today.
- `vela-mcp`, `vela-rag`: MCP SDK (6.3 MB); sqlite-vec is a platform-specific native module, so an install failure only affects RAG.
- `vela`: pi-tui and the CLI.
- memory, web, permission-gate have no heavy dependencies, so they stay in core as built-in extensions, but **use only the public extension API** (as pi's built-ins do). That proves the extension API is sufficient, lets #218 rebuild memory without touching core internals, and makes moving them out later a folder move.

## Couplings to undo first (checked on main `d224386`)

1. `src/vela.ts` constructs `ChannelGateway`, validates `channelIdleMs`, wires `onSaved → gateway.sessionSaved`, exposes `channels()` / `startChannels()`, stops the gateway on dispose; `src/extensions/runner.ts` calls `gateway.register(channel)`; `src/cli/serve.ts` reads `velaInternals(vela).gateway`. Replace with the smallest generic core surface (for example start/stop hooks for extensions and a session-saved event) and move the gateway into `vela-channels`. This is the main design work; name every new core export.
2. `memory` imports `channels/scope` to tell group memory apart: make "scope" a generic session property in core that channels fill in.
3. `config/settings.ts` imports MCP config types: each extension declares its own settings section.
4. Built-ins and the Feishu adapter import core internals (`vela-session`, `tools/registry`, `messages`, `logger`, `custom-message`, `images/metadata`, `channels/scope`): each one becomes a deliberate public export of core or channels, or is replaced by an existing public API. List them all.
5. `src/index.ts` statically re-exports feishu, mcp and rag. After the split, `@glows777/vela` re-exports them; `@glows777/vela-core` does not.

Out of scope: new extension events for memory (for example a generic "session ended" hook for automatic extraction). #218 decides that after measurement. Also out of scope: renaming the user-facing `feishu` extension name, settings keys or tool names; only the package is called `vela-lark`. If the plan proposes renaming those too, list it separately as a breaking change.

## The plan must answer

1. The new public API of `vela-core` and `vela-channels`, export by export, and why each is needed.
2. What happens to `vela.startChannels()`, `vela.channels()`, `channelIdleMs` and the `feishu` / `mcp` / `rag` exports from `@glows777/vela` (keep via re-export, move, or break; breaking changes go in the CHANGELOG).
3. How the checks below are implemented (reuse knip/madge or a small script like pi's), and how they run in CI.
4. Where tests go (per package or root), how `bun run test`, typecheck, build, `smoke:consumer` and `scripts/eval/` run afterwards.
5. Differences from pi's layout, with reasons.

## Checks to add (permanent)

- Each package imports only the packages it declares; dependency direction only points down; no cycles between packages.
- Importing `@glows777/vela-core` loads none of the Feishu SDK, MCP SDK, sqlite-vec or pi-tui; importing `@glows777/vela-channels` loads none of them either.
- One public-API snapshot test per package (today there is one for everything).

## Steps

1. Plan on this issue; Claude reviews.
2. PR: undo the couplings above in place and add the checks (behavior unchanged).
3. PR: move into `packages/*`, update imports, build, release script, CI, `scripts/eval/`. Moves only; while it is open no other PR merges.

## Acceptance

- The checks above pass in CI.
- In an empty project, installing only `@glows777/vela-core` pulls none of the Feishu SDK, MCP SDK or sqlite-vec.
- Existing `@glows777/vela` imports, the `vela` CLI and `vela serve` behave as before (or the CHANGELOG lists each break); `bun run test`, typecheck, build pass; `bun run smoke:consumer` passes for every package in Node and Bun; `scripts/eval/` still runs.
- Quality ratchet stays green.

Design notes: `direction/later-design.md` section "拆包" in the project files.

items.title: Add guided first-run model setup before TUI session startup
items.body:
## Approved product choices for the first delivery

**The maintainer approved the following three choices. This section supersedes the earlier pending-decision wording and the earlier proposal to omit a connection-test action.** The previously approved Rust `inquire`, frontend ownership, and pre-full-screen-TUI interaction boundary remain unchanged.

1. **Provider scope:** DeepSeek guided setup plus an explicit custom configuration route for other providers, proxies or self-hosted endpoints. Do not expand the initial guided template list incidentally. Exact DeepSeek endpoint/model/profile values must still be verified against primary documentation during implementation; approval of the provider family is not verification of a particular model alias.
2. **Credential storage:** recommend local configuration-file storage by default, while also offering a reference to an existing environment variable. Clearly disclose that a locally stored key can be read by the agent's filesystem tools and may enter tool history/model context. Do not edit shell startup files or add an OS-keychain integration in this delivery. Preserve masked input, safe diagnostics and the previously specified non-destructive/private-file persistence requirements.
3. **Connection test:** provide an explicit, optional test action. Before sending it, disclose that it connects to the chosen provider and may incur a small charge. Never test automatically, and never require a successful test to enter the TUI when local prerequisites are satisfied. On failure, offer correction, an explicit retry, skipping the test, or exit. Do not automatically retry, switch providers, or send a user's chat message as an undisclosed probe. Skipping establishes only local configuration readiness, not verified authentication or connectivity.

Consequently, the older statements that no provider request can occur before the first chat message now have one narrowly defined exception: a user explicitly requested this disclosed connection test. Update implementation acceptance cases accordingly: no automatic request on launch/save, one request per explicit test/retry action, skip without a request, clear failure recovery, and no forced passing-test gate. The implementation must specify test execution and recording without leaking credentials or fabricating a user conversation; the library choice does not settle that implementation detail.

These are approved product requirements, not a claim that implementation, provider verification, testing or installation has been completed. Preserve the user's original conversation intent throughout the guide. The issue remains open.

---

## Maintainer decision: frontend-owned command-line onboarding using Rust inquire

**This decision takes precedence over conflicting wording in the earlier proposal below.** The maintainer confirmed the interaction boundary and selected the Rust `inquire` library (`mikaelmello/inquire`, crate `inquire`). This is not authorization to use the similarly named C++ library, add a JavaScript runtime, or redesign runtime startup.

- **Product owner of the flow: the Lattice frontend/TUI executable.** When startup prerequisites are missing, guide the user step by step rather than merely print an error and exit. Ask only for missing information; an already configured launch proceeds normally.
- **Run the guide before the full-screen TUI.** Use ordinary-terminal, Inquirer-style sequential prompts through Rust `inquire`. When the user finishes, restore/release the prompt terminal state and enter the real TUI in the same process; alternatively the user may choose to exit. Do not construct an empty conversation or enter the full-screen interface merely to host the guide.
- **Reuse configuration logic, not the existing full-screen form as the interaction shell.** Reuse applicable catalog parsing, validation and safe persistence beneath the prompts. The advanced/custom configuration route is also a pre-TUI question flow, not a prerequisite visit to an already running TUI.
- **#60 is the product delivery workstream.** #61 supplies only concrete enabling changes needed by this flow, such as returning a missing-configuration result instead of unconditionally exiting, preserving launch intent, and correct startup/cleanup ordering. A separately completed general shared-startup API or cross-host lifecycle refactor is not a prerequisite.
- Keep the previously specified protections: no destructive catalog reset, no silent provider/conversation switch, no premature empty ledger/workspace, explicit partial-save results, and safe credential handling. Noninteractive/background and model-free use must not be forced through this guide.
- Select and pin a compatible Rust library version during implementation, inspecting its actual prompt, cancellation, password and terminal-restoration behavior. Add focused checks for prompt cancellation/interrupt and handoff into the TUI. The library choice alone does not prove those behaviors have been integrated correctly.

**Still proposals, not approved by this selection:** the first guided provider/model list, default credential storage policy, and whether to offer an explicit connection test. The earlier DeepSeek/local-key/no-automatic-probe recommendations remain recommendations. Do not infer their approval from the choice of interaction library.

No implementation or dependency installation was performed when recording this decision. The issue remains open.

---

> **Reading order and status:** The concrete proposal appended below answers and narrows the original review questions; the original body is retained as background. This is an implementation handoff proposal, not an approval or completion claim. The provider/template and no-automatic-probe recommendations in #60 require maintainer confirmation before that scope ships. The issue remains open.

## Problem

A new user cannot reach the existing model-entry form until a model is already configured. The desired interactive path is: open Lattice, choose a supported provider/model, enter a credential, and start chatting—without first learning environment variables, JSON, adapter dialects or endpoint/model identifiers.

This issue owns the first-run user experience. Shared startup responsibility and error boundaries are a separate, related design issue; this must not become an all-runtime refactor.

## Verified current behavior

Baseline: develop `8d5a829e5c0a34bfe54829acf3e24b982e57c418`, compared with remote main `edd25b0d7d669428abce0cee1e57e2b7d5413268`.

- `src/bin/lattice/startup.rs:10-69`: `config()` calls `PresetConfig::from_env()`, then `require_key()`. Missing credentials cause diagnostics and `std::process::exit(1)`, before the interactive setup UI can run. This file is identical on the two compared branches.
- `src/view.rs:199-269`: `ModelForm` already accepts six fields: short name, dialect, model, endpoint, literal API key, or key-variable name. These are an advanced configuration form, not provider-led onboarding. `model_actions.rs:167-198` can save with `Option<&Session>` set to `None`; only the audit notification is conditional on a live session. Existing `model_controls/tests.rs` covers saving without a session. The form itself is therefore not blocked on a whole-runtime redesign.
- `src/models.rs`: catalog persistence and literal-key loading already exist. Literal keys become generated environment-variable references before adapter configuration is constructed. The Unix staged-file writer attempts mode `0600`, but discards the permission-setting error; it must not be described as an unconditional guarantee.
- `docs/getting-started.md:25-70`: the main setup path requires manual directory/catalog creation and shell key export. Its content is unchanged between the compared branches.
- `LATTICE_SCRIPTED=1` bypasses the model requirement, but is a deterministic test mode, not the intended real-model first-run experience.

### Additional catalog findings to scope explicitly

`models::add_to` currently replaces a parsed, non-object `models` value with an empty object (`src/models.rs:321-328`), despite refusing malformed JSON and unreadable files. This is an existing preservation defect, not a reason to claim all invalid catalogs are already protected. `require_key` also exits before `report_catalog`, and existing startup tests fix that ordering. Record the required fixes explicitly or split them into linked follow-ups; do not hide a catalog rewrite inside onboarding.

### Isolated reproduction

Ran the existing local debug binary, reporting `v0.1.0-dev+gc21f8ba93c32`, with a fresh temporary HOME and working directory, a minimal environment with no model credentials/configuration, and closed stdin. It exited before entering the TUI:

```text
exit: 1
no model this installation can reach.
  the model catalog is empty
Created files: []
```

The startup/configuration source paths used for this finding have no diff from that commit to the reviewed develop head. This was a process-level startup check, not an interactive UI acceptance test and not a live provider request. No personal configuration, installed binary or running session was changed.

## Desired outcome and proposed acceptance criteria

- [ ] With no catalog and no key, interactive TUI launch shows setup rather than terminating with instructions to hand-edit JSON.
- [ ] The approved guided provider/model path asks for credentials without requiring the user to type a dialect, endpoint or model identifier. Keep a clearly separate advanced/custom-endpoint route.
- [ ] Saving valid setup lets the same launch enter a real chat session; a subsequent launch can reuse the saved choice without shell exports.
- [ ] Missing credential, malformed/unreadable catalog, invalid form data, unwritable storage, and remote authentication rejection have distinct, actionable feedback. Local key presence is not presented as successful remote authentication.
- [ ] Cancellation leaves existing configuration intact. Invalid/unreadable catalogs are never treated as empty and overwritten.
- [ ] Credential input remains masked; key values do not enter startup diagnostics or audited adapter configuration. Explain that storing a literal key on disk is not protection against agent file reads or immutable tool-result logging. Verify the intended file-permission behavior, including errors.
- [ ] Existing configured users, explicit model choices, documented preference fallback and scripted mode continue to work. Noninteractive/daemon startup must not unexpectedly enter a terminal wizard.
- [ ] Add isolated first-run/process tests, deterministic form/error tests, and a recorded human TUI acceptance. Keep English and Simplified Chinese getting-started guides aligned.

## Decisions needed before implementation

1. Which provider/model choices are supported by the first guided path? Where do their explicit templates come from and how are they maintained? Do not silently invent endpoints or credential-variable names.
2. Is a preflight connection check part of setup, or is authentication feedback delivered on the first chat request? A check can use the network and incur cost; it must be an explicit product choice.
3. Define the minimal common startup error interface needed by the guide, in the linked boundary review. Reuse existing catalog/persistence capabilities rather than duplicating their rules in a wizard.

## Non-goals

No OAuth/account system, marketplace, provider billing integration, automatic catalog seeding with unreachable models, credential transfer to another provider, or redesign of every model-management panel. Provider templates, if approved, are not automatically enabled catalog entries. Do not restart a running session or overwrite an existing user's preferences to make onboarding appear successful.

---

## Concrete first-run proposal and implementation handoff

This section defines the proposed flow and its error behavior so it can be implemented without the original discussion. It does not change the kernel or make a large startup refactor a prerequisite. Consume #61's narrow prerequisite-check slice; reuse the existing catalog and form persistence logic after its preservation defects are fixed.

### Product decision requiring maintainer confirmation

**Recommended first delivery:** one guided provider family, DeepSeek, plus the existing advanced/custom-endpoint route; no automatic network connection test in the wizard. Credentials are validated locally for presence/shape, then the first explicitly submitted chat request supplies real authentication feedback. The reason is a complete small first-run journey without pretending to support every provider or sending a possibly billable request before the user asks a question.

This is a concrete recommendation, not a record that the maintainer already selected the provider list or approved a network probe. Confirm or replace this row before shipping the guided provider choice. The rest of the flow and the #61/persistence work do not require a new provider decision. If the maintainer chooses a connection-test button later, it is a separately explicit, disclosed network operation, never a hidden startup probe.

Candidate template: the existing OpenAI Chat Completions adapter, DeepSeek's documented endpoint, and a verified Flash-family model/profile. The repository already has `profiles/deepseek-v4-flash.json` and DeepSeek endpoint references; they are evidence of existing integration, not proof that a live offering or alias is unchanged. The relationship between current and legacy Flash-family aliases must be checked in the official source; do not relabel one model with another model's profile by assumption. The template PR must record the exact accepted model ID, endpoint root and profile from primary provider documentation, and a separately authorized smoke test. If that evidence cannot be obtained, do not ship a guessed guided template. Keep the advanced route explicit and mark the guided delivery incomplete.

### Template ownership, not bundled active models

Use a small versioned setup-template data file owned by the product configuration layer. Each template contains a stable template ID, display provider/model names, exact adapter/model/base URL, a compatible profile reference or inline validated profile, official source URLs and last verified revision/date. Adapter code does not infer these from marketing names. Templates are shown only as choices; they do not create reachable catalog entries or appear as configured models before the user saves one.

No runtime provider-directory fetch, automatic model enumeration, account login, pricing table or guessed credential-variable name. Templates change through reviewed data updates, with English/Chinese documentation kept in sync. Tests use synthetic endpoints/keys; a stale or missing template produces an unavailable choice with a reason, not fallback to another provider. Primary references: `https://api-docs.deepseek.com/` and `https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing/`; research search results are pointers, not a substitute for the template PR's full verification record.

### Entry conditions and ownership

- Start the bootstrap view only for an interactive TUI launch whose chosen chat configuration has a repairable prerequisite problem. Do not enter a terminal wizard for daemon/noninteractive input, scripted mode or model-free embedded use.
- Preserve the original launch intent: working project, fresh/latest/named conversation, explicit model override and tool workspace. As specified in #61, resolve latest/named to an existing target read-only before the wizard and retain that target even if a newer conversation appears. No empty Session, ledger or configured tool workspace is created just to show setup.
- An already reachable configuration launches normally. Missing credentials for an explicit choice show that choice's problem first; changing it requires the user's explicit selection, not an invisible provider fallback.
- A saved preference still follows the existing documented fallback policy. Temporary fallback does not overwrite that preference. An override selected inside setup is clearly for this launch if an external environment/launcher choice will still win next time.
- Reuse the existing advanced form for custom endpoints. This issue owns a guided wrapper and pre-session host, not a duplicate catalog implementation or a redesign of all model panels. First-run Ink/daemon onboarding is not added incidentally; their existing configured startup must remain intact. TUI is the acceptance target named by this issue.

### Flow and state machine

```text
check prerequisites
  -> ready: existing startup
  -> repairable: choose provider/template or advanced entry
       -> enter credential/storage choice
       -> review selected provider/model and storage warning
       -> Save and start
       -> persist -> recheck chosen configuration -> existing session build
  -> unreadable/invalid required catalog: explain -> retry after repair or cancel
```

The guided path asks only for provider/model choice, a short local entry name (with a usable suggested name) and credential. It does not ask the user to understand an adapter dialect or type an endpoint/model identifier. Duplicate entry names require choosing a different name in this flow; no implicit replacement of existing entries. Editing a specific existing entry to repair its credential is a distinct explicit action that preserves its provider/model/endpoint and other fields.

Default guided storage recommendation: **save a literal key locally**, with a visible explanation and explicit Save action, so a fresh user can relaunch without shell exports. Offer an alternative “use an existing environment variable” for users who already manage credentials. Do not create or edit shell startup files. Do not invent an OS keychain integration in this scope. The key input is masked, never echoed in the review summary or diagnostics, and cleared from the form after successful handoff or cancellation. Clearing the widget is not a promise of cryptographic memory erasure.

Review displays provider, model, destination catalog path, credential storage mode and whether the choice is persisted as the preferred model. State plainly: a literal key is on disk in an agent-readable file; filesystem-tool results may put it into immutable history and model context. Existing chat redaction is not protection for arbitrary reads of this file. Do not promise that saving a key makes it inaccessible to the agent.

The primary action is “Save and start,” not “Verify account.” No provider request occurs until the first user-submitted chat message. Saving establishes local configuration only.

### Persistence and failure rules

1. Distinguish nonexistent catalog from malformed/unreadable/non-object catalog. Only the nonexistent case creates a new catalog. A valid root containing a non-object `models` member must be rejected, fixing the current `add_to` preservation defect.
2. For a valid catalog, preserve all unrelated entries and fields, including entries with diagnostic problems. Do not normalize the whole file into a reduced schema that drops unknown content.
3. Re-read and compare the catalog version immediately before a staged write. Serialize participating writers; if the file changed externally, report a conflict and reload rather than overwriting the other edit. Document the ordinary local race guarantees; do not claim a sandbox against malicious same-user writers.
4. Write via a unique staged file on the same filesystem and atomic replacement. Create it exclusively, never reuse an existing temporary path, and on Unix request a mode no wider than `0600` **at creation**; verify the resulting mode before writing any credential bytes, not merely before publishing. On write, permission-check or replacement failure, close and remove only this operation's temporary file; if cleanup fails, report its safe path and the fact that sensitive residual data may remain, never its contents. The prior catalog stays intact. Do not ignore chmod/cleanup errors or announce saved. This promises the checked Unix mode, not immunity from ACLs, administrators or arbitrary same-user tools. On platforms without the required protected-writer guarantee, literal-key persistence remains unavailable and the environment-reference option is explicit.
5. Reuse existing literal-key-to-generated-environment-reference conversion before creating adapter configuration. Literal values must not appear in startup diagnostics, audit-facing adapter configuration or readiness messages. This is not a new guarantee that later agent file reads are redacted.
6. Catalog and preference storage are two separate resources. Save the catalog first, then the explicitly chosen preference. If preference saving fails, report “model saved; default selection not saved” and offer an explicit continue-with-this-model for the current launch or retry the preference write. Do not roll back a successfully saved model or silently claim a cross-file transaction.
7. A successful save is followed by a fresh #61 check using the approved current-launch selection, not a stale previous configuration. If construction subsequently fails, keep the saved configuration and explain the actual startup problem; do not restore an older key or delete the new entry automatically.
8. Cancel before save changes neither catalog nor preferences and creates no conversation/workspace. Cancel after a successful save does not secretly delete the saved model; display that it remains available for the next launch.

After save, the same process continues into the requested conversation; no restart is required. If the requested resume target is unavailable, report that specific problem rather than silently starting a fresh conversation. Restore terminal state on every cancel/failure exit.

### Failure matrix and recovery

| Failure | User sees / next action |
| --- | --- |
| Empty key or missing/empty referenced variable | Local validation error; no file write or network request |
| Malformed form/template or unsupported adapter | Field/template diagnostic; remain in setup |
| Bad/unreadable catalog | File problem with path; edits disabled; retry after external repair or cancel |
| Name conflict | Pick another name or enter the explicit existing-entry repair flow; never replace silently |
| Concurrent catalog edit | Explain conflict, reload choices, retain masked unsaved input where safe; do not blindly retry write |
| Directory, permission or staged-write failure | Existing file remains unchanged; retry only after explicit user action |
| Preference write failure after catalog success | Partial success is named; explicit continue/retry as above |
| Provider rejects first actual chat request | Existing structured runtime failure; provide a route back to model/credential settings. Do not assert which credential field is wrong solely from generic upstream text |
| Network/rate/provider failure on first request | Keep saved configuration, present the actual call failure; no automatic setup rewrite, provider switch or audited-call retry |

Credential correction after the session has started reuses model management; any resend is explicit. A late authentication failure does not rerun setup as an automatic loop or repeat the original message unseen.

### Delivery slices and dependencies

1. Land #61 S1: recoverable prerequisite results and explicit host behavior. Do not wait for an all-runtime redesign.
2. Fix catalog-shape preservation, checked permissions and conflict-safe staged writes in focused persistence work; protect existing model-management callers with the same tests.
3. Add pre-session TUI hosting and the guided template/credential/review flow, plus the existing advanced route. Approval/evidence for the first provider template is a release gate for the guided path, not a reason to guess values.
4. Connect Save and start to the existing lifecycle with preserved intent and partial-save handling. Update both getting-started guides.
5. Record human TUI acceptance with an authorized real account; automated fixture success is not live authentication or usability acceptance. Keep this issue open until that record exists.

### Acceptance tests a new implementer can write immediately

- Isolated HOME/project, no catalog/key: interactive startup reaches setup; closed stdin/noninteractive daemon does not enter a wizard. No personal configuration is read or changed.
- Existing reachable configuration and scripted mode skip setup. Explicit bad selection never silently switches provider; preference fallback is preserved.
- Synthetic guided template fills exact adapter/endpoint/model/profile without asking for those fields; advanced route accepts explicit custom values without guessed defaults.
- Masking, safe errors, no network request before chat submission, and no key value in adapter configuration/diagnostic output.
- Missing catalog creation; malformed JSON, non-object `models`, unreadable file, unrelated fields/entries, duplicate names and a concurrent edit. A poison version that turns invalid content into an empty catalog must fail the regression.
- Exclusive temporary creation, private mode before any credential bytes, a pre-existing temporary-path collision, staged write/permission/replacement failure, and temporary cleanup failure preserve precisely the states above. Check both the newly created staging file and published mode with synthetic credentials. A poison writer that writes the key before establishing permissions must fail; cleanup-failure diagnostics must report residue without printing it. Preference-save failure is tested separately.
- Cancel before/after save, terminal cleanup, same-process entry into chat, fresh/latest/named selection, and a second launch reusing the saved preference when no explicit external override supersedes it. While the wizard is open, create a newer conversation and prove that the captured latest target does not change; remove the captured target and prove startup errors instead of creating Fresh.
- Simulated first-call authentication and transport failures retain configuration and require explicit repair/retry; no hidden probe or automatic resend.

Public code anchors: `src/bin/lattice/startup.rs`, `lifecycle.rs`, `model_actions.rs`, model controls/forms, `src/models.rs`, `src/view.rs`, `src/preset.rs`, `tests/startup_trace/preflight.rs`, model-controls tests and the English/Chinese getting-started guides. The initial research baseline remains `8d5a829`; inspect the actual checkout before editing.

### Planning review record

Source behavior was checked against public-repository baseline `8d5a829`. Independent takeover reviewers examined the proposal, and a final cross-plan consistency review found no remaining handoff blockers after corrections. Explicit maintainer approval gates remain in force. This records planning review only: no implementation, test execution, provider request, installation or current-session restart was performed for this planning task. Implementation PRs must supply their own focused and negative-control evidence.
